unsure: (1) The predicate is 'a Try with non-empty catches, not inside a DefDef, ImplDef or Function': consistent with uncurry, which does not lift try/finally; try/finally-only and synchronized shapes verify on base and are left alone. A catch whose cases all throw or return also verified before and now gets a local too (bytecode change, still valid). (2) The new local is owned by Eraser.this.context.owner and the boxed tree is changeOwner'd to it, following gen.evalOnce's use of context.owner in the same class; a lambda and nested labels inside the try run correctly, but a reviewer should confirm context.owner is the right owner in every position box can be reached from (field initialisers never reach it: uncurry lifts every try there). (3) Delambdafy's TypeAdapter gets localOwner = localTyper.context.owner only to satisfy the new abstract member; its adaptations never hold a try. (4) Bound shapes no longer have the patmat Block/LabelDef directly under the box, so posterasure's new-C(e).underlying peephole and the back end's match shapes do not apply to them; those methods were invalid before. (5) Textual conflict with retronym/scala#526 (erasure rewrite: replaces the Eraser's and Delambdafy's anonymous TypeAdapter with ErasureTypeAdapter / typedCast); it would need localOwner from its transformer's currentOwner. retronym/scala#643 edits unbox in the same file, a separate hunk. (6) The run test needs the 'unreachable code' warning in its check (the constant-false guard is what stops patmat making a switch, as in the finding).
note: Erasure's box of a derived value class now stores an argument containing an un-lifted try/catch in a fresh local before `new C(local)` (for a Unit-underlying class, the expression is evaluated as a statement first); every other box is unchanged.
